en: The Great Amulet Dhāraṇī;
the Noble Great Amulet Dhāraṇī:
Om! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Great Amulet!

Homage to the Buddha! Homage to the Dharma! Homage to the Saṅgha! Homage to all the Tathāgatas! Homage to all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present! Om Vipulagarbha, Vipulavimale, Vimalagarbhe, Vimale, Jayagarbhe, Vajrajvālāgarbhe, Gatigahane, Gaganaviśodhani, Sarvapāpaviśodhani!

Oṃ Guṇavati! O you who move through the sky, O you who move through the sky! Giri, giri, giriṇi, giriṇi! Gabhari, garddhabhari, gamari, gamari, gabhari, gabhari! Gaha, gaha, gargāri, gargāri, gagari, gagari, gaṃbhari, gaṃbhari, gabhi, gabhi, gahi, gahi, gamani, gamani, guha, guha, guru, guru! (Mpv-Dh_131)
Guruṇi cale, mucale, samucale; guhaṇi-guhaṇi, guruṇi-guruṇi; culu-culu, cale-cale, mucale;
Jayavijaye, Jayavati, Aparājite; Sarvabhayavigate, Sarvagarbhasaṃrakṣaṇi; Siri-siri, bhiri-bhiri, miri-miri, giri-giri, piri-piri; Samantākarṣaṇi, Sarvaśatrūn pramathani; protect, protect me!
And for all sentient beings at all times, from all fears, all calamities, and all diseases: *cili-cili viri-viri dhiri-dhiri*, O Purifier who removes obscurations, Destroyer of manifold obscurations!

*muci-muci muri-muri muli-muli kili-kili mili-mili*, O Kamalā, O Vimale-vimale (Stainless One), O Bearer of Victory and Triumph, O Victorious One, O Distinguished One, O Blessed One, Wearer of the Jewel Crown and Garland, Wearer of many various and diverse garments!
O Blessed One, Great Knowledge Goddess, protect, protect me and all sentient beings on every side, O Purifier of All Evils!
Hulu-hulu, mulu-mulu, protect, protect me and those among all sentient beings who are without a protector and without refuge!
Deliver those who have no jewels, no refuge, and no ultimate resort from all sufferings!
O Caṇḍī-Caṇḍī, Caṇḍinī-Caṇḍinī, O you who possess speed, O repeller of all the wicked, O bearer of victory!
Huru-huru, curu-curu, turu-turu, O protector of life!

O crusher of the best of gods, honored by all the hosts of deities! Ciri-ciri, viri-viri, O you who look upon all things! Prabhe-prabhe, O you of beautiful radiance, O you of pure, beautiful radiance! O you purified of all evil, O purifier of all evil! Dhuru-dhuru, O bearer of the earth! Dhara-dhara, O well-guided one, O well-sounding one! Ru ru!
Move, move all the wicked; fulfill our hopes!
O Māttaṅginī, bearer of the glorious body, Jayakamalā, Kṣiṇi-Kṣiṇi, you who hold the boon-bestowing goad!
Om, Padmaviśuddhe, purify, purify! Pure one, pure one! Support, support! Bhiri-bhiri! Bhuru-bhuru! O Maṅgalaviśuddhe!

O Pure-faced One! O Wielder of the Sword! Khaḍgini! Khaḍgini! Khara-khara! O You whose crest is ablaze! Jvalita-śikhare! O You whose radiance is observed from all sides! O Suprabhaviśuddhe! O You who are purified by light spread forth everywhere! Blaze! Blaze! O You who attract the hosts of all gods! O You whose vow is truth! Oṃ hrīṃ traṃ! Cross over! Cross over! Deliver me, O Blessed One, and deliver all sentient beings! O Nāgavilokite! Quickly! Quickly!

Lahu-lahu, hulu-hulu, hutu-hutu, turu-turu, tuhu-tuhu, kiṇi-kiṇi, kṣiṇi-kṣiṇi, devourer of all grahas, piṅgari-piṅgari, mucu-mucu-mucu-mucu, sumu-sumu, well-shaking one, tara-tara, O beholder of the nagas, save me, O Blessed One, and all sentient beings from the ocean of saṃsāra, O Blessed One, from the eight great terrible fears!
Everywhere, in all directions, with the binding of the vajra-noose, O Vajrajvālinī, purified by vajra-flames!
Bhuri-bhuri bhara-bhara bhiri-bhiri bhuru-bhuru, O Blessed One, purified in the womb, purifier of pride, filler of the belly, protectress, protector! Blaze, blaze! Move, move!
Oṃ Jvālinī!
May the deity rain down divine water from all sides; O you who rain down nectar, you who descend as a deity, may she consecrate me with the nectar-body of the sublime speech of the Sugatas.
Protect, protect me and all sentient beings everywhere and at all times from all fears, from all calamities, and from those terrified by the fear of all malevolent beings;

O purifier of all strife, quarrels, disputes, and every fear; O purifier of evil dreams, ill omens, inauspiciousness, and sin; O fulfiller of the womb; O shatterer of all yakṣas, rākṣasas, and nāgas; Bala, Bala, Balavatī! Jaya, Jaya, Vijaya, Vijaya!
May it be victorious everywhere and at all times! May this great vidyā be accomplished for me! Accomplish the maṇḍala!
Strike down obstacles! Victory, victory! Be perfected, be perfected! Awaken, awaken! Fulfill, fulfill! O Fulfiller, Fulfiller!
Fulfill my hope, O you whose form has arisen like the moon; victory, O supreme victor, O bringer of victory, O victorious one! Abide, abide, O Blessed One; observe your vow.

O you who are the purity of the heart of all Tathāgatas, look upon me and all sentient beings, and completely fulfill all hopes. Protect all sentient beings, and protect me from the eight great terrible fears! Move, move! Spread forth, spread forth, O purifier of all obscurations!
O you who are pure in every aspect, who have departed, departed, and are free from stain; O purifier of all stains, purified by all auspiciousness!
Kṣiṇi, kṣiṇi, O you who purify all evil! O you who are free from impurity, victorious one, radiant one, adamantine one!
Vajre vajravati | oṃ trailokyādhiṣṭhite svāhā | sarvatathāgatamūrdhābhiṣikte svāhā |
Adhiṣṭhita by the heart of all Tathāgatas, O Heart, svāhā!
Accomplished in the samaya of all Tathāgatas, svāhā!
O Indra, O Indravatī, O Indravyavalokitā, svāhā!
Svāhā! To Brahmā, who dwells in the Brahman, svāhā! To that which is empowered by all the Tathāgatas, svāhā! To that which is honored by Viṣṇu, svāhā!
Svāhā to her who is saluted and worshipped by Maheśvara! Svāhā to her who is empowered by the strength and heroism of Vajradhara Vajrapāṇi!
Svāhā to Dhṛtarāṣṭra!
To Virūḍhaka, svāhā!
To Virūpākṣa, svāhā! To Vaiśravaṇa, svāhā!
Svāhā to the one honored by the Four Great Kings!
Svāhā to Yama!
Svāhā to the one honored and saluted by Yama!
Svāhā to Varuṇa!
Svāhā to the son of Varuṇa!
Svāhā to the Maruts!
Svāhā to the great wind!
Svāhā to Agni!
Svāhā to Vāyu!
Svāhā to the Nāga-gaze!
Svāhā to the hosts of gods! Svāhā to the hosts of nāgas!
Svāhā to the hosts of yakṣas! Svāhā to the hosts of rākṣasas!
Svāhā to the hosts of gandharvas!
Hail to the hosts of epilepsy!
Hail to the hosts of asuras! Hail to the hosts of garuḍas!
Svāhā to the hosts of kinnaras!
Svāhā to the hosts of mahoragas! Svāhā to the hosts of humans!
Svāhā to the hosts of non-human beings!
Svāhā to all the seizing spirits (grahas)! Svāhā to all the lunar mansions (nakṣatras)!
Svāhā to all beings!
Svāhā to all pretas! Svāhā to all piśācas!
Hail to all those afflicted by epilepsy!
Hail to all the kubhāṇḍas!
Hail to all the pūtanas!
Svāhā to all the kaṭhapūtanas!
Svāhā to all the wicked and malicious ones!
Oṃ dhuru-dhuru svāhā!
Oṃ turu-turu svāhā / Oṃ kuru-kuru svāhā / Oṃ curu-curu svāhā /
Oṃ muru-muru svāhā!
Oṃ hana-hana all enemies svāhā! Oṃ daha-daha all malevolent ones svāhā!
Oṃ paca-paca [burn, burn] the adversaries and enemies, svāhā! Those who wish me harm—set ablaze, set ablaze the bodies of all those with malicious minds, svāhā!
To the vajra-flame, svāhā!
Svāhā to Samantajvāla!
Svāhā to Maṇibhadra! Svāhā to Pūrṇabhadra!
Svāhā to Samantabhadra! Svāhā to Mahāsamantabhadra!
Svāhā to the Mothers of Space!
Svāhā to those who go to the ocean!
Svāhā to those who roam by night! Svāhā to those who roam by day!
Svāhā to those who roam during the three junctions of the day; svāhā to those who roam at the appointed times;
svāhā to those who roam outside the appointed times.
Svāhā to those who take away the embryo!
Svāhā to those who sustain the embryo! Svāhā to those who carry away the embryo!
To those who bear the embryo, svāhā!
Calu-calu, svāhā!
Hulu-hulu, svāhā!
Oṃ svāhā!
Bhūḥ svāhā! Bhuvaḥ svāhā!
Svaḥ svāhā! Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! Cili-cili svāhā!
Dharaṇī svāhā!
Dhāraṇī svāhā!
Of Agni, svāhā!
Tejovāyū svāhā!
Cili-cili svāhā! Sili-sili svāhā!
mili-mili svāhā / budhya-budhya svāhā / maṇḍalabandhe svāhā /
Svāhā! In the binding of the boundary, svāhā! Subdue all enemies, svāhā! Render them senseless, render them senseless, svāhā!
Paralyze, paralyze, svāhā!
Cut, cut, svāhā! Pierce, pierce, svāhā!
Shatter, shatter, svāhā!
Bind, bind, svāhā!
Delude, delude, svāhā!
Svāhā to the pure jewel!
Svāhā to the sun, the pure sun!
Svāhā to the purifier!
Viśodhani svāhā!
Candre-candre pūrṇacandre svāhā!
Grahebhyaḥ svāhā!
Svāhā to the constellations!
Svāhā to the piśācas!
Svāhā to the auspicious ones!
Svāhā to all! Svāhā to the peace-bringers!
Svāhā to the nourishers!
Svāhā to those who provide auspiciousness! Svāhā to those who remove the fetus! Svāhā to the bringer of peace!
O bringer of peace, svāhā! O bringer of nourishment, svāhā!
O increaser of strength, svāhā!
Śrīkari svāhā!
Śrīvardhani svāhā! Balavardhanakari svāhā!
Śrījvālinī svāhā!
Muci svāhā! Namuci svāhā!
Vegavati svāhā!
Oṃ svāhā!

O you who are the embodiment of all Tathāgatas, O most excellent one free from attachment, O Blessed One who has transcended fear, may there be well-being for me from all evils, and may there be well-being for all sentient beings, svāhā!

Oṃ muni-muni vimuni-vimuni dhari-dhari cari-cari valane bhagavati bhayaharaṇi-bhayaharaṇi bodhi-bodhi bodhaya-bodhaya budhiri-budhiri cuṃbili-cuṃbili svāhā / To you who are cherished by the hearts of all Tathāgatas, svāhā!

Oṃ muni muni munivare, consecrate me and my retinue, as well as all sentient beings, with all the Tathāgatas’ empowerments of all vidyās, sealed with the great armor-seal, O pure one empowered by the hearts of all Tathāgatas! Seal! Vajra! Svāhā!
This is the Aparājitā Great Dhāraṇī, the heart of the Great Seal, the wish-fulfilling jewel vibrating with the purity of a garland of universal flames.
Furthermore, there are these other mantras, which are perfected, auspicious, and effective for all rites; they grant every desire. Bhadra spoke: "Listen!"
Namely: Oṃ amṛtavare varavara pravara viśuddhe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ amṛtavilokini garbha saṃrakṣaṇi ākarṣaṇi hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā / This is the Heart Mantra of Aparājitā.

Oṃ vimale vipule jayavare jayavāhini amṛtaviraje hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā / Oṃ bhara bhara saṃbhara saṃbhara indriye balaviśodhani hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ ru ru cale svāhā / Oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā /
The Upahṛdaya-vidyā:
by the mere hearing of this, all sins are destroyed.
Homage, repeated homage to her, joined with whom one possesses a vajra-body! Homage, homage!
Homage, homage to her, remembering whom Rāhula, while still dwelling within his mother’s womb, protected her when she was cast into the river of poison. Homage, homage to her!
Salutations again and again to her who protects the merchant’s son when he is intent on slaying a cruel serpent, and who [protects him] from the burning of poison... and so forth.
Salutations always to her by whom the great king Brahmadatta was protected, so that Aṣṭaka, having conquered his enemies, became preeminent.
Homage, repeated homage, to her by whom the immoral monk was bound by the neck with disease and released from life, and by whom he went to heaven.
Homage, homage to her whom the caravan leader called to mind as a protector of the merchants' lives when their ship was tossed about in the ocean. Homage, homage to her!
Homage, repeated homage to her, by whom, while his wife was thus bound, the king obtained a son with arms outstretched! Homage, homage!
Remembering her poverty, she gave a dīnāra to the Jina; the King was pleased and declared her a donor: "Homage to her, homage again and again!"
Salutations, salutations to her, by whom the Lord, the wielder of the thunderbolt, though bound by the awakened Asuras, obtained victory through his crest-jewel. Salutations, salutations!
Homage, repeated homage, to her who, having fulfilled the six perfections solely through the power of compassion, conquered the Māras and became the Victorious Buddhas.
Salutations, repeated salutations to her, by remembering whom even a criminal deserving of death was completely liberated when cast into every kind of peril.
Salutations again and again to her, by whom the leader of the city, though his throat was bound, was released from the peril of his means.
And this Aparājitā-vidyā, which is upheld by all the Buddhas,
is constantly sealed, spoken, recited, and demonstrated by others.
Written down, rejoiced over, honored always for the benefit of sentient beings,
and remembered by being applied to the body— to her, homage, homage again!
Salutations again and again to her, the mere hearing of whose name is difficult to attain in the three worlds, and likewise the recitation or study of it.
This knowledge, difficult for even Buddhas to obtain, has been prophesied and highly praised;
it is renowned as a great dhāraṇī that brings about the destruction of all evil deeds.
Possessing great strength, great serpents, great splendor, and great radiance,
this knowledge (vidyā) is endowed with great qualities and is the destroyer of all Māras.
She shatters the conspiracies of evil, liberates one from the intoxication of Māra,
is the mother of the Bodhisattvas, and destroys all that is wicked.

She is the protectress, the nourisher, the sustainer, and the destroyer of supreme mantras; she is the auspicious goddess who brings about the total destruction of *kākhorda* spells and the application of poisons.
And for those who delight in the Mahāyāna, as well as for those who receive [this teaching], write it down,
perform its recitation and study, and constantly uphold it— let it be heard!
And one should always bestow upon others that which has been cultivated in the mind,
having placed it within a book and honoring it with worship and salutation.
She who removes all evils, auspicious, and who fulfills the equipment for enlightenment—to her, homage; to her, homage; to her, homage; homage, homage!
By the power of whose mantra all fears and calamities,
as well as wicked asuras, humans, daityas, gandharvas, and rākṣasas [are overcome].
Planets, Skandas, epileptic spirits, Piśācas, Yakṣas, Kinnaras,
hosts of Ḍākinīs and Śākinīs, Nāgas, diseases from above and below,
various fevers, and likewise ailments caused by the magical rites of others.
Poisons, fire, weapons, spells, lightning, the afflictions of time,
excessive rain, drought, and all fears of enemies.
Likewise, other calamities as well will undoubtedly perish;
all undertakings are accomplished—homage to her, homage again and again!
And whoever shall bear that vidyā upon the neck, the arm, or the head,
the gods, daityas, nāgas, and humans will protect him constantly.
Gandharvas, kinnaras, yakṣas, bhūtas, pretas, piśācas,
ḍākinīs, rākṣasas, messengers, kumbhāṇḍas, and kaṭapūtanas.
Whoever should recite this constantly at the three junctions of the day, they will always be protected by the Buddhas,
as well as by the Pratyekabuddhas, the Śrāvakas, and the Bodhisattvas of great supernatural power.
Yogins who have mastered mantras, great ṛṣis of immense power,
Vajrapāṇi the lord of yakṣas, and Śakra together with the gods of the thirty-three realms.
The four great kings, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Nandikeśa, Mahākāla, Kārttikeya, and Gaṇeśvara.
The Bhairavas, the Mātṛkās, Durgā, and likewise other deities belonging to the host of Māra,
as well as the Vidyā-devis of great heroism, possessing great strength and prowess.
Māmakī, Bhṛkuṭītārā, Aṅkuśī, Vajraśṛkhalā,
Mahāśvetā, Mahākālī, Vajradūtī, and Upāśikā.
Vajramālā, Mahāvidyā, Suvīryā, Amṛtakuṇḍalī, Vajrāparājitā, Caṇḍī, Kālakarṇī, Mahābalā,
as well as Dhanyā, Mahābhāgā, and Padmakuṇḍalī.
Maṇicūḍā, Puṣpadantī, Svarṇakeśī, Piṅgalā, the great goddess Ekajaṭā, Dhanyā, and Vidyutsumālinī.
Kapālinī and Raṃ (Laṃ) Keśī, Kṣudrākṣī as the sole leader,
Hārītī, Pāñcikā, Śaṅkhinī, and Kūṭadantinī.
Śrī Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, Siddheśvarī, who is ever-following.
Others also protect that very person in whose hand this knowledge resides;
he shall be intent upon the liberation of all sentient beings.
Kings shall come under his control, and he shall increase his mass of merit;
all ritual procedures will be accomplished once he has entered the temple of the Jina.
A woman who maintains this vidyā shall go before the feet of the Buddha, just like the word of the Jina; and when pregnant, she shall give birth easily.
A woman without a son obtains a son; freed from disease, she enjoys happiness;
endowed with wealth, grain, and excellent things, she becomes honored and speaks kindly.
"It makes true dreams and one shall attain the field of the Victors.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, and that entire assembly rejoiced. Thus it was said.
The Noble Mahāpratisarā Vidyā-dhāraṇī is completed.
